notes: Title as ink: Carte régulière (orientée) du polygône régulier P_n (n≥2). Manuscript page 111 at lower left. No date or second hand is visible. The sheet is a handwritten mathematical note, not a reused typescript.

Every prose line, the initial set-difference formula, both rows and three vertical relations of the upper diagram, the six arrows of the first lower diagram, the four arrowheaded connections plus one plain segment of the enclosed diagram, and the final labelled map were compared with both witnesses. Agreement in C/H was not treated as evidence by itself.

The initial three-position key gives sommets at the upper-left star, centres faces at the lower-left star, and milieux arêtes at the right star. A tiny dark dot above the right star is copied graphically as an uncertain dot; its incidental or formal meaning is not decided. Specks outside the ink were not promoted to text or punctuation.

The first upper-row target has three stars and four punctures 0,∞,1,-1. The next target has one star and two dots. Most later two-star forms also have a third right-hand dot; H frequently drops one position. These are local mathematical changes, not differences between prose description and TikZ.

The two vertical isomorphism signs each have a separate wavy and straight stroke. Both are reproduced as a 90-degree rotated simeq; the intermediate equality is two straight upright strokes. The source distinction is graphical and does not introduce a different mathematical operation.

The upper centre quotient is visibly /D_n without a +; it is not repaired to /D_n^+. The first lower central numerator Sigma is visibly unindexed, as is the left numerator in the enclosed diagram. The enclosed bottom numerator has n while its denominator has 2n. All are retained even where uniform notation or the subgroup interpretation would suggest another form.

The cancelled fragment under upper-right division remains uncertain as par le. In the left note a separate cancelled de is retained before isomorphisme. The multiply struck D-shaped group is retained as uncertain D_n; its subscript is not reconstructed from the replacement D_2n.

The final note reads de la ramification sous les arêtes in the enlarged crop. Sous is a source reading, not an interpretation of the geometry. The final tout has a very long shared t crossbar and compressed middle strokes; no separate cancellation is seen, and no unambiguous tt abbreviation is asserted.

The bottom-left target subscript 1 has a thick left entry. No independently readable cancelled n is isolated, so a cancellation has not been invented. The upper-left star on Sigma_1 in the enclosed middle row is retraced but live.

H’s editorial opening note, Diagramme de quotients heading, sic marker and explanatory notes are not manuscript prose. Its notes are nevertheless used to assess concrete diagram content: H acknowledges the enclosing contour and the unindexed central quotient, so those are not blanket H omissions. Its displayed upper middle equation conflicts with its own note about the vertical parallel relation. No separate H drawing files were supplied, so only the available text/TikZ descriptions are collated.

The only use of mathematics beyond reading was the explicitly conditional checks below. Neither check supplied an absent plus, subscript, star, or word. In particular they do not settle the four-position decoration or a/alpha subscript.

Main reader independently inspected all nine crops and agreed with the four-position enclosed decoration, final de la ramification sous les arêtes, early Sigma_3, and unindexed numerator nodes. Following that crop-backed adjudication, the marginal index is narrowed to a/alpha, the tiny initial dot is explicitly uncertain, and both vertical isomorphism signs use the actual two-stroke rotated-simeq geometry.

check_events.statement: Conditional standard dihedral model: in G=C_(2n) semidirect C_2, A=<r>, B=<r^2,s>, C=<r^2> satisfy A∩B=C, AB=G and all four relevant indices equal 2.
check_events.place: Two lower quotient diagrams; identification with D_2n, D_2n^+, D_n and D_n^+ is conditional on the intended group convention.
check_events.outcome: Actually enumerated pairs (k,e) with product (k+(-1)^e l mod 2n,e+f mod2) in Python for n=2,...,8. Verified A∩B=C, AB=G, [A:C]=[B:C]=[G:A]=[G:B]=2, and normality of C by left/right coset equality. Orders were (4n,2n,2n,n). This is a finite check of the conditional subgroup pattern, not proof of the manuscript’s group convention or covering assertions.

check_events.statement: Conditional puncture count for the two-faced regular n-gon model: removing vertices, edge midpoints and face centres removes n+n+2=2n+2 points, equal to removing the vertices and face centres of the 2n-gon model.
check_events.place: Initial three-star definition and the displayed isomorphism Sigma_n^(three stars) ≃ Sigma_2n^(two stars plus dot).
check_events.outcome: Checked by counting the n vertices, n edge midpoints and two faces: n+n+2=2n+2. This supports the stated pattern only under the two-faced model and does not decide any doubtful individual ink mark.

math_risks: The early upper central quotient is /D_n without plus while the later four-puncture quotient is /D_n^+. This is a source tension under the standard subgroup model; no plus was supplied.
The enclosed left numerator has four separated decoration positions and no subscript, unlike the neighbouring three-position notation. The fourth glyph remains unresolved.
The enclosed bottom numerator is Sigma_n while its quotient group is D_2n. The source index is retained rather than harmonised with the other lower-left quotient.
The index of barred Sigma in the upper-right note remains a/alpha uncertain; its intended object cannot be inferred securely from this page alone.
